note: Every ad is tagged on 5 dimensions before launch so a win can be explained. Concepts are per campaign (campaign.json). Add a value here before using it; the linter rejects unknown tags. Codes go into the ad name, so keep them short and never reuse a retired one.

angles.never-miss: Every visitor gets an answer; nobody leaves unseen (copy: "A full-time, always-on SDR that never misses a website visitor.")
angles.speed: Speed-to-lead: answer and book while the buyer is still on the page
angles.wasted-traffic: Traffic you already paid for leaves without a word
angles.buyer-experience: What the buyer sees: they ask, it answers ("Go ahead. Ask me stuff.")
angles.attention: Attention is earned, not interrupted: inbound beats interruption
angles.follow-up: The visitor left; Breakout follows up by email and LinkedIn
angles.integrations: It talks to your stack; you touch grass
angles.humour: A joke about something the persona already cares about, then the product
angles.identify: See which companies and people are on your site before they fill a form (the free trial: Signals)
angles.contract: Switching cost: the contract, the renewal, the buyout that removes it
angles.go-live: Time to live: hours, not an implementation project
angles.signals: What you can see about a visitor and account: signals, people, not just the account
angles.outcome: Meetings booked, not leads qualified: the outcome, not the step before it
angles.incentive: A gift for taking the demo: lowers the cost of the first meeting
angles.vendor: Who builds and supports it: shipping weekly, working with the builders

personas.demand-gen: Head of demand gen or growth marketing: owns the website's conversion and the MQL to meeting number
personas.markops: Marketing operations: owns the martech stack, enrichment, routing and CRM data quality
personas.practitioner: Demand gen and marketing ops in one audience, for small lists (a company list) where splitting by role would starve each campaign
personas.cmo: CMO or VP marketing at a B2B software company: owns pipeline targets and headcount; buys the full product through a demo
personas.founder: Founder or CEO of a startup that sells to businesses: buys alone, decides fast
personas.revops: RevOps or marketing ops: owns the stack, routing and the CRM
personas.sales-leader: VP sales or head of SDRs: owns speed-to-lead and the SDR team

awareness.unaware: Does not know the problem exists. Lead with something they already care about
awareness.problem: Feels the problem (traffic that leaves, slow follow-up). Name it, then the turn
awareness.solution: Knows AI SDRs exist. Show what makes this one different
awareness.product: Knows Breakout. Show proof and the product up close
awareness.most-aware: Ready to act. The offer and the CTA, nothing else

img-1x1.note: Single image, square. The default in feed

img-wide.note: Single image, 1.91:1. Desktop feed and the right rail

img-4x5.note: Single image, vertical 4:5. Mobile feed only

doc.note: Document ad: a swipeable PDF, 3 to 6 pages

video-motion.note: Motion design from a video template (particle-swarm, dot-matrix, swiss-grid) cut to 6 to 15 s

video-creator.note: A real person talking to camera (team member or a creator who signed a release). The engine writes the script

thought-leader.note: Thought Leader Ad: a member's own post (Sachin, the team, or a creator) sponsored from the company page

hooks.verdict: A short, confident claim in the brand's words
hooks.question: A question the persona already asks themselves
hooks.joke: A joke about the persona's world
hooks.proof: The product doing the thing, up close
hooks.contrast: Today versus with Breakout, 2 to 4 words a side
hooks.pov: First person: the buyer's or the marketer's point of view
hooks.pattern-break: Looks like nothing else in the feed (a struck-through form, one notification in empty space, a near-empty field): stops the thumb by breaking the pattern, then lands the concept

competitors_note: Matched as whole words, case-sensitive. Vendors whose names are everyday words (Default, Outreach, Unify) are left out to avoid false alarms: check for them by eye.
